answer: To defend against sybil attacks, the system uses an identity-bound relic receipt mechanism. Each agent establishes a unique thread to the network, forming an oasis of trust. Upon receipt submission, verifiers cross-check against the oasis. If a sybil tries to clone, they lose the 100 relic tokens invested in establishing their thread, as the network rejects duplicate receipts. This costs more to clone than they gain, ensuring economic deterrence.
